Retain the locked Laravel/Vue 3/strict TypeScript/Inertia/MySQL 8.4/Tailwind 4.1/shadcn-vue/Reka 2/TanStack 8/ECharts 6/VeeValidate 4.15.1+Zod 3 families and exact arithmetic/codec/runtime selections from Architecture §6. Resolve exact supported stable patches/digests at bootstrap with lockfiles and strict peers. No Pinia initially, Redis/Horizon/broker, permissions/workflow engine, separate API/frontend deployment, generic repository platform or new chart/calendar engine is planned.

Phase 2 payroll, overtime compensation, performance appraisal, recruitment/ATS, benefits and multi-company tenancy stay excluded. No salary/bank/national-ID/medical-document field, facial recognition, identity guarantee, continuous tracking, public registration or role impersonation is added. All generic fixtures/evidence are synthetic.

The blueprint is refined in two dependency-driven ways: its single persistence group becomes G-008–G-011 to preserve the schema’s exact interleaved 90-table order with tested slices, and cross-module clocks/leave/temporal coordination plus real Shared control contracts have separate backend groups. This produces 33 groups. Every migration slice is followed by meaningful MySQL checks; no commit creates all 90 tables or all 44 screens. Owned module Actions/readers may be tested before full feature exposure, but incomplete cross-module mutation adapters stay absent/closed. The later activation task is explicit; there is no successful production stub or event-based repair of an invalid committed state.

Workforce trusted effective readers and Analytics dirty-state contract are implemented early in G-011 because Identity authorization and all source-changing workflows consume them. They are real read/owned-write contracts over already-created storage; they do not recursively invoke authorization or create another module. Shared operational UI remains within existing appropriate Identity/admin or feature composition paths, backed by Shared contracts; no seventh business-module directory is required.

## 4. Git Workflow Strategy

- Protect main. Normal work never commits directly to main and never force-pushes it. No permanent develop/release/hotfix branch is introduced.
- Each group has exactly one named branch, created from the current verified main only after its preceding group PR is merged. Fetch main and fast-forward the local base; do not branch from an unmerged feature tip.
- Each task produces one coherent Conventional Commit containing its complete subtasks/tests/status update. A subtask creates no independent commit.
- Open one PR per group after all its task commits pass their gates. Owner review and required CI precede integration.
- Use GitHub merge-commit integration with squash disabled for these PRs. Preserve task commits and their IDs; the merge commit is an integration record outside the planned task-commit count.
- Verify deterministic required checks on the merged main SHA, record the group PR/merge reference, then create the next group branch from that updated main.
- Save/reopen/close the .pen asset before switching branches. Resolve design conflicts in the actual editor, preserving IDs; do not mechanically repair serialized object IDs.
- A task-only instruction authorizes only that task’s bounded work/commit. A group instruction may cover its ordered tasks and PR preparation. Review/merge/publish/release actions require their stated actual authorization/gates; no unrelated next task starts automatically.

Routine command sequence, performed only in a later authorized execution repository:

1. Read the selected group’s exact branch field and verify previous group merge/main checks.
2. Run `git status --short`, `git fetch origin`, `git switch main` and `git pull --ff-only origin main` when origin is the verified remote.
3. Create the exact group branch with `git switch -c <exact branch from group table>`; the angle text here denotes a lookup, not an allowed branch placeholder.
4. Execute the selected task’s ordered steps, required checks and scoped staging. Use its exact subject and review `git show --stat --oneline HEAD` after commit.
5. At group close use the §25 PR template and merge-preserving method; verify main before continuing.

The repository must already have an initialized main containing the source baselines and this plan. No hidden genesis/extra implementation commit is assumed. [T-0001](#t-0001) is BLOCKED if the owner has not selected/provided that execution repository.

## 5. Development Hierarchy and Naming Conventions

| Element | Stable identity | Git or evidence mapping |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Development phase | Phase 0–Phase 6 | Logical milestone; all constituent groups merged plus milestone exit evidence. No phase branch. |
| Task group | G-000–G-032 | Exactly one unique type/gNNN-kebab-case branch and one reviewed merged PR. |
| Task | T-0001–T-0280 | Exactly one atomic task commit with ID in its Conventional Commit subject. |
| Subtask | Ordered unchecked step inside a task | Completed within parent commit; no independent commit. |
| Screen | Unchanged UI-* source ID | Saved frame/state/viewport/revision approval; does not imply a new route or task commit by itself. |
| Verification ID | Original AC/INV/VQA/ADR/DBD/BR/OD/WF ID | Trace to tasks and actual check/evidence path; not an invented product requirement. |

Use lowercase kebab-case branch descriptions, PascalCase PHP/Vue classes, source module namespaces and consistent lower-case Inertia page directory casing on Linux. Existing reviewed code locations take precedence within the task’s bounded scope; inspect them before creating another file. Migration filenames use ordered creation names/timestamps chosen at execution while preserving §23.1 table order. Listed glob/directory scopes are bounded permissions to implement one named contract, not authorization for broad refactoring.

<a id="sec-06"></a>

## 6. Task and Commit Identity Conventions

Commit convention: `<type>(<scope>): <verb-oriented increment> (T-NNNN)`. The exact expanded subject appears in every inventory row and task field. Allowed planned types include docs/design/chore/feat/test/perf. Group PR titles identify G-NNN and preserve included task IDs/SHAs. Task IDs remain stable when text is refined; reviewed plan amendments introduce new unique IDs and update the entire dependency/coverage/count registers without renumbering accepted task commits.

Every task includes Title, Description, Objective, Parent Group, Dependencies, Source References, Expected Files, concrete Subtasks, Acceptance Criteria, Tests/Verification, exact Git Commit, task-specific Definition of Done, Risk/Notes and Status. The per-task Expected Files automatically includes only that task’s status/evidence row in TASK.md. No separate checkbox-only commit is allowed.

Before committing, record DONE intent/status and tested commands in the same scoped task commit only after verification. The resulting SHA cannot be embedded in its own commit. Record it in PR/execution metadata, then reconcile group evidence when available; do not amend old approved commits to fill self-references. Never record a planned subject as evidence that its commit already exists.

<a id="sec-07"></a>

## 7. Dependencies and Strict Sequential Execution

At most one group is ACTIVE and one task IN_PROGRESS. The documented order is a total sequential execution order: G-000 → G-001 → … → G-032 and T-0001 → T-0002 → … → T-0280. Each immediate predecessor is mandatory; explicit additional dependencies below reference earlier tasks only. No critical work is planned in parallel.

| Dependency kind | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| Group dependency | G-N depends on G-(N−1): preceding PR merged, integrated main checks passed and fresh branch base recorded. |
| Task dependency | T-N depends on T-(N−1) plus any listed earlier tasks: verified predecessor task commits exist before start. |
| First task of group | Requires both preceding task completion and preceding group merge; a verified feature-tip commit is insufficient. |
| UI readiness | Relevant .pen frame/state/viewport approval plus completed real backend contract precede UI slicing. |
| Future verification | A later check is an explicit activation/follow-up obligation, never an unseen prerequisite for an earlier task or a claimed pass. |

## 8. Definition of Ready

- Locate the task and group in this version of TASK.md and read relevant current approved sources, module contracts, repository instructions and existing code/tests.
- Confirm the owner instruction covers this task or ordered group; unrelated continuation is not authorized by completion.
- Verify every earlier task dependency has actual passing evidence and a task commit. For a new group verify previous PR merge and current integrated main checks.
- Check exact group branch/base and a clean working tree. Do not discard unrelated user work to become clean; isolate or report the precise conflict.
- Confirm allowed files, source IDs and acceptance conditions; inspect existing components/services to avoid duplicate abstractions.
- Confirm real required module contracts, migrations, actor/generation context and disposable test resources exist. Do not invent missing dependencies.
- Before a UI task, locate explicit approved .pen file/frame/revision/state/viewport evidence and actual backend DTO/action contracts.
- Check source fingerprints and the accepted G-000 attendance resolution; an unapproved changed rule/architecture/persistence/design contract blocks affected work.
- Identify executable tests/quality-pack activation and the exact later follow-up for a genuinely unavailable check.
- If a prerequisite is missing, mark this task BLOCKED with source IDs, smallest resolution and preserved work; do not skip to another task.

<a id="sec-09"></a>

## 9. Definition of Done

Task completion requires all ordered subtasks checked, task-specific observable acceptance passed, all already-applicable required checks passing, current permission/history/transaction/privacy rules intact, no unrelated changes/secrets, reviewed diff, exactly one task commit and recorded evidence/status. Failure or unknown required evidence means incomplete work.

Group completion additionally requires every task DONE with its preserved commit, group acceptance passed, branch CI, actual owner review where stated, no blocking defect, reviewed PR merged by merge commit, and required checks on integrated main. A branch containing code is not a MERGED group. Each task’s final checklist steps belong to its same atomic commit; no independent subtask or tracking commit is added.

Phase completion requires all listed groups MERGED and the roadmap exit evidence. Phase 1 additionally requires all 44 explicit screen approvals; Phase 6 additionally requires actual SIT/UAT/release acceptance and all REL gates. Neither a design approval nor a merged group implies stable MVP release.

Before a check activates, record NOT_YET_APPLICABLE with the reason and named activating task from §23, then run it at activation/group close. A suite that exists and fails is not not-yet-applicable. Do not disable tests, reduce source acceptance, suppress failed samples or bless unrelated snapshots to finish a commit.

## 13. Phase 0 — Documentation Readiness Tasks

This phase contains [G-000](#g-000). All groups start NOT_STARTED and all tasks start TODO. Follow the total order in §11–§12.

<a id="g-000"></a>

### G-000 — Documentation Baseline Readiness

| Group field | Planned contract |
| --- | --- |
| Group ID / title | G-000 — Documentation Baseline Readiness |
| Development phase | Phase 0 — Documentation Readiness |
| Exact Git branch | `docs/g000-baseline-readiness` |
| Branch type | docs |
| Base branch | Current verified main from owner-selected initialized repository |
| Group objective | Establish execution authority, resolve the attendance projection concern and freeze source references without changing business definitions. |
| Relevant modules | All six modules |
| Source references | PRD §1, §14.1, §24–§25; Architecture §1, §15, §26; Schema §11.5, §20, §23; Design System §2, §18, §30 |
| Previous group dependency | None; execution repository entry prerequisites |
| Expected deliverables | 4 verified task increments: Verify repository entry and authoritative source approvals; Adjudicate attendance punctuality and completeness projection; Record the approved minimal source correction and refresh stale citations; Freeze documentation and planning execution references |
| Technical risks | Architecture has established-baseline metadata rather than explicit owner approval; Design System embeds stale schema status/hash; attendance state representation remains to be adjudicated. |
| Owner review | Owner confirms architecture acceptance if no authoritative approval record can be located; owner reviews any actual schema-contract correction. Existing PRD/schema/design approvals are retained. |
| Group verification | DOC plus all activated §23 task/group packs and exact targeted checks specified in each task; on main use Architecture§24.3 integrated suite. |
| Pull Request title | docs(g-000): Documentation Baseline Readiness |
| Merge prerequisites | Every task DONE/committed; group acceptance and required CI passed; actual required owner review; no blocker; reviewed diff; merge preserves individual task commits; verify integrated main before next group. |
| Group status | NOT_STARTED |

**Group acceptance criteria**

- All four source versions/hashes and genuine approval evidence are recorded.
- Late and early departure can coexist and inconsistent completeness has an explicit lossless contract.
- Only the smallest owner-reviewed source correction, if required, is accepted before affected migrations.
- No application, design screen or execution task is marked implemented.

## 21. Design Screen-to-Task Coverage

There are 44 primary source major-view IDs: Identity 7, Workforce 7, Scheduling 5, Attendance 7, Leave 10, Analytics 3 and Shared 5. Each has exactly one primary authoring task and one primary implementation task. Representative screens are authored in G-002 and reused, not counted again. A view may share a route/component or be a focused review section.

**Initial screen approval status: DRAFT — not authored.** No frame/node/revision/asset commit is invented. During design fill the actual file/frame path, tool-provided node ID when available, saved revision, covered viewport/state list, owner decision/date and asset/approval commit reference in this register or its PR-linked evidence. Until actual APPROVED evidence exists the relevant UI task is BLOCKED at Ready. All references use `design/phase-1/professional-hris.pen`.

## 22. Database and Invariant Coverage

### 22.1 Exact 90-table creation ownership

The order below is copied from the selected Schema §23.1 and checked against all 221 declared FK parents. Every table appears once. Every assigned migration task includes actual dictionary sections/types/keys/CHECKs/NO ACTION parents, real invalid/duplicate/history fixtures and MySQL verification. Self-FKs are legal in their own table; every other parent precedes its child. No constraints are disabled. Framework-managed migrations repository is reconciled, not created twice. A G-000 accepted state correction updates affected dictionary/count expectations before execution.

A pack is mandatory only after its listed activation, and an existing applicable failure always blocks completion. No later check is silently assumed green.

Earlier bootstrap notes it NOT_YET_APPLICABLE and this task replays the applicable prefix. |

This is progressive applicability, not a waived failing gate.

### 23.1 CI trigger and merge/release obligations

| Level / trigger | Blocking checks | Evidence / scope |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Task | All target checks plus applicable formatting/static/types/build/architecture and relevant authorization/history/transaction/fault checks. | Exact command/output/result, source/design reference and one task commit; no unrelated full rerun after already-passing checks without new changes/failure/concern. |
| Pull request | Locked dependency/platform/peer/secret audit; Pint/PHP static; TS/lint/build; Unit/Feature/Architecture; targeted MySQL races; critical Playwright/private/demo paths. | Actual applicable branch CI; owners review scope/constraints/approval evidence; future-only runtime gates remain visible. |
| Main | Repeat deterministic required checks on merged SHA, complete available MySQL concurrency/browser/migration smoke; build immutable image; only then controlled synthetic staging and operational smoke. | Protected main status and preserved task/merge commits. No failing required check can be merged away. |
| Phase | All groups merged plus roadmap milestone; Phase 1 explicit 44-frame approvals, backend real invariant contracts, frontend functional/visual state coverage. | Milestone review and accepted references; no percentage substitutes for incomplete required work. |
| Release candidate | Full traceable SIT/UAT by persona; supported-browser genuine capture/accessibility evidence; BR-28; retention/security/fault exercises; isolated DB/file/current-control restore and observed RPO/RTO. | Current accepted code/config/source/design/evidence. Failed required checks/targets remain blockers. |
| Stable release | All REL-001–REL-008 satisfied, critical defects closed, owner release acceptance and verified integrated main; annotated v1.0.0. | Preserve exact tag/merge SHA/images/evidence/config. No Phase 2 work before stable Phase 1 acceptance. |

Destructive migrate:fresh/reset/purge/restore/load commands may run only after explicit disposable environment/database/private-volume/dataset identity checks. Never point them at real/unknown data or production secrets. EXPLAIN ANALYZE executes SELECTs and must use the isolated representative fixture. Generic portfolio fixtures use no real employees, real visitor photographs/GPS, tokens or production data. Concurrency uses MySQL 8.4 and production isolation/constraints.

Runtime evidence can remain applicable across a later documentation-only commit only when application/dependency/image-runtime inputs, schema, configuration and dataset equivalence are explicitly recorded. Do not report a benchmark/device run as newly executed on that SHA; rerun relevant evidence if those inputs changed. Required deterministic main checks still run on the integrated merge SHA.

## 24. Codex CLI Execution Protocol

Example owner instruction: `Execute Task T-0042 according to docs/phase-1/TASK.md.`. Locate that exact task and its group; the example does not authorize a later task.

### 24.1 Scoped Context Loading

For each selected task, load the complete context needed to execute and verify that task. Use stable section/group/task anchors and bounded line ranges from the current file; do not repeatedly load this entire large document or every source document into context.

| Context slice | Required content | Loading and refresh rule |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Active task | The complete selected task block: metadata, parent, dependencies, source references, allowed files, every ordered subtask, acceptance criteria, verification, Definition of Done, planned commit and evidence fields. | Locate the exact task anchor with `rg -n`; derive its current bounds from the next task, group or top-level section anchor and read the complete block. An inventory row or summary is insufficient. |
| Parent group | Group objective, exact branch, prerequisites, source references, risks, owner review, acceptance, Git commands, PR title, merge gates, status and ordered task inventory. | Read the group's metadata, acceptance criteria, inventory and Git command/PR/merge blocks wherever they are located. Load another task's detailed block only when it is an actual dependency or its contract/evidence is needed. |
| Dependencies and sequence | The active task's dependency entries, matching rows in §11–§12, actual predecessor task commits, previous group merge/current-main evidence and the contracts produced by those dependencies. | Verify completion against current repository/evidence. Follow further ancestors only where a prerequisite, contract, failure or ambiguity requires it; do not recursively reload the entire completed backlog. |
| Global execution rules | Applicable repository instructions; §1–§9 for authority, scope, Git, identity, sequence, Ready and Done; §23–§28 for checks, execution, PR/merge, blockers, tracking and risks. | Load these rules at session entry and retain a compact working summary with exact section references and content fingerprints. On a document/repository revision, inspect the diff and refresh changed or affected slices before relying on the summary. |
| Relevant source and coverage | The task/group's cited sections and IDs in PRD, Architecture, Schema and Design System; relevant rows of §20–§22; applicable approved .pen frame/revision and existing owned contracts, code and tests. | Read current authoritative passages, including linked rules, invariants, constraints, workflow/acceptance details and technical prerequisites needed for the task. Load adjacent or cross-module sections when they affect correctness. |

Keep a compact in-session context manifest containing the selected task/group, exact branch and planned commit, verified dependency evidence, loaded section/source references and fingerprints, applicable gates and unresolved blockers. Reuse unchanged verified slices during that session; refresh the active task and any changed dependency/source/rule slice when switching tasks or resuming after context loss. A cached summary is a navigation aid and cannot establish approval, completion or a passing check by itself.

If a passage is truncated, a source reference is missing, rules conflict or a cross-module implication is unclear, expand the relevant context until the issue is resolved or record the specific blocker under §26. Never infer an omitted subtask, acceptance criterion, permission or business rule from a title alone. A task requiring a comprehensive baseline or cross-document audit must still perform that full audit; scoped loading limits repeated context consumption, not verification depth.

G-000 remains the mandatory first gate, including Architecture approval verification, attendance state-contract review and the necessary Schema-reference refresh. Scoped loading does not waive source authority, strict sequencing, approved design references, test applicability, owner review or any Ready/Done/merge/release gate. It requires no additional project document.

### Before execution

- Apply §24.1 Scoped Context Loading to read the selected task in full, its parent group, verified dependencies, applicable global rules and relevant current source passages; identify the exact branch, allowed files and acceptance.
- Verify owner execution scope, previous task commits and previous group merge/main checks before creating or selecting a branch.
- Inspect clean working tree, current code/tests/ports/components, source hashes and actual installed package/tool versions.
- Confirm .pen frame/state/viewport/revision owner approval for UI and real completed backend collaborators; never use a generated preview as approval.
- Identify executable exact check commands and explicit activating/follow-up tasks for unavailable progressive checks.

### During execution

- Execute this task’s checklist in order as one coherent reviewable increment using existing conventions and owned boundaries.
- Keep authoritative rules in server services/workflows and current authorization at every entry/query/field/file/delivery boundary.
- Use one workflow transaction, ordered anchors, expected version, same intent, critical audit/outbox/source invalidation and private evidence semantics.
- Add or update meaningful relevant tests with the implementation; inspect full changed implications for history, economics and concurrency.
- Stay inside scope; no opportunistic refactor/framework/dependency/Phase 2 addition or silent source reinterpretation.
- On a real blocker preserve safe work, mark BLOCKED and report exact source/prerequisite plus smallest resolution; do not fabricate a successful service or skip to an unrelated task.

### After execution

- Run target and every applicable shared gate; inspect actual results rather than claiming checks from code presence.
- Review diff, file scope, secrets/sensitive data and task acceptance; failed required work is incomplete.
- Update the task evidence/status in the same atomic commit, stage only intended files and use its exact planned subject.
- Record the actual resulting SHA in PR/task execution metadata; do not add a status-only second commit or amend old approved commits for self-references.
- Report task ID/group/branch/commit, meaningful changes/tests/limitations and next dependency-eligible task.
- Stop at the user-selected scope. A completed task does not authorize execution of the next task; an explicitly authorized group may continue sequentially within that group.
- When group scope is complete, prepare its one PR and follow §25. Actual review/merge/deployment/release gates remain applicable.

<a id="sec-25"></a>

## 25. Pull Request and Merge Protocol

Each group ends in one PR from its exact branch to protected main. Use this template inside the PR; it is embedded here and no standalone PR template file is created by this assignment.

> **Group:** ID/title; phase; objective.  
> **Branch/base:** exact branch; main base SHA and predecessor merged PR.  
> **Included tasks:** ordered IDs, exact commit subjects and actual SHAs.  
> **Sources:** unchanged requirement/BR/OD/WF/AC/ADR/INV/DBD/UI IDs and accepted document/frame revisions.  
> **Behavior/change:** concrete resulting increment and relevant before/after consequences.  
> **Files/schema:** bounded scope, migration positions/parents/constraints, additive/compatibility/backfill/rollback impact.  
> **Security/history:** current authorization/field/private-file, employment/economic/retention/generation implications.  
> **Verification:** exact commands/results, targeted/full applicable CI, negative/race/fault evidence; NOT_YET_APPLICABLE reason and named follow-up where genuine.  
> **Design evidence:** exact approved .pen file/frame/revision/covered states/viewports, safe screenshots/differences where relevant.  
> **Group acceptance:** each group condition pass/fail with evidence; blocking defects/limitations/remaining risks.  
> **Owner review:** actual decision/date and scope; no prefilled approval.  
> **Merge readiness:** all tasks one-commit/DONE, no blocker, required checks passing, task history preserved.  
> **Post-merge evidence:** merged PR/merge SHA, integrated-main checks, next eligible group.  

- Use merge-commit PR integration; do not squash task commits into an indistinguishable feature commit or force-push main.
- Do not merge failing required checks or unsigned material design/architecture/source changes. Reviewers judge the actual bounded result and relevant evidence.
- Preserve the task subjects/SHAs, source/evidence links and historical design references needed for release traceability.
- The merge commit is an integration record outside the 280 task-commit count. Record group MERGED only when the PR really merges and main checks pass.
- Fetch/verify main after merge, record its base for the next exact group branch, and start no next group from the old feature tip.
- For G-032, create annotated v1.0.0 only as the authorized post-merge integration action after actual release acceptance and current required main/equivalence checks. The tag does not create another implementation task commit.

<a id="sec-26"></a>

## 26. Blockers and Change Management

Routine local implementation choices within accepted architecture are allowed: variable/helper names, small internal placement, component composition and fixture organization. They do not require new owner approval. Preserve the already-authorized task scope.

| Review required for actual change | Reason / affected boundary |
| --- | --- |
| Business behavior, MVP modules, permissions or leave economics | Update approved source through owner decision before dependent implementation. |
| Attendance evidence/time/GPS behavior or historical meaning | Cannot weaken original evidence, independent review or employment/occurrence interpretation. |
| Transaction/ownership/module architecture deviation | Affects synchronous invariants/import DAG; review relevant ADR and tests. |
| Destructive schema migration or material persistence correction | Protect accepted history/economics, obtain accepted smallest migration/source change and safe rollout. |
| Significant operational third-party dependency/provider addition | Verify need/compatibility/custody/operational burden; do not silently introduce another service. |
| Material departure from approved frame or source-state contract | Get a concrete revised approved reference and keep previous approval history. |

Blocked-task protocol: preserve the working tree safely; identify task/source IDs and exact missing decision/resource/contract; record BLOCKED plus smallest resolution; provide a concrete reviewable correction; resume only after resolution. Do not erase unrelated work, substitute a stub, rename a failed state to success or auto-advance another group.

If real defects require new work beyond the current atomic task, amend TASK.md through a reviewed bounded planning change: allocate new stable IDs, insert a valid execution position, recompute every affected earlier-only dependency/unblock/branch/commit/trace/count entry, and keep accepted IDs/SHAs unchanged. New tasks must have the same full template. An emergency narrowly scoped reviewed fix branch pauses normal group work and is an explicit approved plan exception, never a hidden extra commit or excuse to start from an unmerged predecessor. This initial inventory contains no fictitious defects, emergency branch or passing repair evidence.

## 28. Technical Risks and Mitigations

| Technical or execution risk | Smallest control / mitigation | Task anchors |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Architecture acceptance metadata absent | Verify actual owner record; request only missing concrete acceptance; do not repeat approved schema/design/OD approval. | [T-0001](#t-0001), [T-0004](#t-0004) |
| Stale embedded schema citations and attendance scalar gap | Adjudicate lossless late+early/inconsistent truth table; owner-accepted minimal source correction if necessary, before evaluation DDL. | [T-0002](#t-0002), [T-0003](#t-0003), [T-0095](#t-0095) |
| Design before application bootstrap has no known Git root | Require owner-selected initialized main containing sources/plan; no hidden genesis branch/commit or unrelated repository write. | [T-0001](#t-0001), [T-0005](#t-0005) |
| Native/framework drift and interleaved FK order | Reconcile exact driver stubs/wire formats; four sequential tested persistence groups preserve 90-table order. | [T-0065](#t-0065), [T-0073](#t-0073), [T-0097](#t-0097), [T-0098](#t-0098) |
| Identity↔Workforce auth recursion / incomplete collaborators | Early trusted read contracts, Shared port binding, module DAG and closed mutation adapters until real coordinator. | [T-0099](#t-0099), [T-0100](#t-0100), [T-0110](#t-0110), [T-0167](#t-0167) |
| Clock timing/codec/SSD/lock misses target | Trusted post-body handoff with queued-FPM trace, bounded native decode outside locks and fixed-host genuine measurements. | [T-0071](#t-0071), [T-0136](#t-0136), [T-0141](#t-0141), [T-0270](#t-0270) |
| Exact half/accrual/period/lineage errors | Typed ticks/BigRational/HALF_UP cumulative postings, per-bucket locks, retained carry/reversal effects and golden/race tests. | [T-0079](#t-0079), [T-0127](#t-0127), [T-0130](#t-0130), [T-0131](#t-0131), [T-0265](#t-0265) |
| Missing/invalid independent route | Explicit same-stage fallback, actual prior actor exclusion, snapshot exception only; invalid first route reserves nothing and later block retains. | [T-0148](#t-0148), [T-0149](#t-0149), [T-0151](#t-0151), [T-0150](#t-0150) |
| Phantom insert or background-only conflict protection | Existing employee anchors/ordered one transaction and fresh owned Attendance/Leave facts; no SKIP LOCKED for business conflicts. | [T-0080](#t-0080), [T-0141](#t-0141), [T-0152](#t-0152), [T-0162](#t-0162) |
| Stale data or old snapshot used as authority | Synchronous source dirty, compare-before-publish, report access/source token and separate fresh RC export checks. | [T-0101](#t-0101), [T-0168](#t-0168), [T-0171](#t-0171), [T-0174](#t-0174) |
| External file/mail/control-store ambiguity | Manifest leases/tombstones, publication-versus-completion, uncertain ACK and protective control quarantine. | [T-0137](#t-0137), [T-0102](#t-0102), [T-0104](#t-0104), [T-0180](#t-0180), [T-0182](#t-0182) |
| Public synthetic fixture leaks into real mode | Dual deployment/dataset guard, no visitor camera/GPS, server fixtures, backend privileged denial, drained epoch reset. | [T-0187](#t-0187), [T-0217](#t-0217), [T-0261](#t-0261), [T-0262](#t-0262) |
| Source approval mistaken for destructive/legal authorization | Unapproved category defaults, actual validation/holds/final checks/current control state and OD-21 real-data gate. | [T-0179](#t-0179), [T-0182](#t-0182), [T-0255](#t-0255), [T-0278](#t-0278) |
| Future checks falsely credited or oversized emergency commit | Progressive gate register, exact evidence, failed means incomplete, reviewed separate atomic plan amendments. | [T-0070](#t-0070), [T-0273](#t-0273), [T-0279](#t-0279) |

## 31. Glossary

| Term | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| Task group | One sequential coherent branch and reviewed merged PR, containing several task commits. |
| Task | One bounded reviewable increment and one exact ID-bearing atomic commit. |
| Subtask | One ordered checklist step inside its parent commit. |
| Verified predecessor | Actual passing task commit; at group boundary also merged PR and current main checks. |
| Main integration record | Merge commit preserving task history; not another implementation task. |
| Design approval | Explicit owner decision for a saved file/frame/revision and covered states/viewports, distinct from Design System approval. |
| Owned Action | Mutation of only the owning module’s state joining the outer workflow transaction. |
| Workflow | Application coordinator enforcing real cross-module invariants synchronously. |
| Stable anchor | Existing company/principal/employee coordination row, including before an empty overlap query. |
| Receipt versus committed result | Technical durable intent/first body time versus successful authoritative business transaction. |
| Exact day unit / tick | Ledger scale 4 day quantity /0.5-microsecond boundary unit; different representations for different purposes. |
| Posted/reserved/available/forecast | Signed posted economics / active commitments / posted minus reserved per bucket / unearned projection unavailable for spending. |
| Current authorization / historical context | Today’s effective scopes/grants versus preserved grouping/evidence at original business time. |
| Source/access fingerprint | Relevant source revisions / current authorized set/fields/generation; neither independently grants access. |
| Control journal/tombstone | Independent acknowledged protective/deletion evidence used for purge/restore reconciliation. |
| Generation | Deployment-bound nonreused epoch invalidating sessions/jobs/artifacts across reset. |
| Planning coverage | A defined implementation/test path; not proof of actual passed behavior. |
| SIT/UAT/release acceptance | Actual integrated scenarios/persona owner sign-off/current REL gates, not document existence. |
